_comment: Single source of truth for macro indicators (Plan A Tier 1). NOT YET wired into index.html render — see PLAN-macro-json.md for remaining steps. Each value carries a 'source' = the FRED / Trading Economics series ID it will auto-fetch from in Tier 2.

us10y.label: US 10Y Treasury
us10y.note: rallied five straight sessions to ~4.81–4.82% (highest since late 2023) on the oil spike + Hormuz war risk, then paused back to 4.79% Wednesday as equities stabilized; Sept hike odds still elevated (~68%, from ~40% two weeks earlier) into the 15–16 Sept FOMC

fedFunds.label: Fed Funds Rate
fedFunds.note: the Fed held on 24 Aug; Jackson Hole plus the Hormuz oil spike have pushed market-implied Sept hike odds to ~68%

usCPI.label: US CPI (YoY)
usCPI.note: August CPI (due before the Sept FOMC) is the key swing input for whether the Fed holds or hikes

usPCE.label: US PCE (YoY)
usPCE.note: not independently re-verified this cycle; watch alongside the CPI print

dxy.label: Dollar Index (DXY)
dxy.note: safe-haven dollar demand holding firm against the same Hormuz war-risk backdrop pushing gold and oil higher

source.caveat: DXY proper is ICE; DTWEXBGS is FRED's broad trade-weighted USD index — close proxy, label accordingly

biRate.label: Bank Indonesia Rate
biRate.note: IHSG (~6,600) and BBCA (~Rp6,550) kept extending straight through the MSCI Indonesia deletion (effective Monday's close) and Tuesday's global Hormuz-driven risk-off

usdidr.label: USD/IDR
usdidr.note: rupiah holding firmer on the BI hike plus continued foreign equity inflows into Indonesian banks, even against a firmer DXY this week

gold.label: Gold (XAU)
gold.delta: slipped, not a haven bid this time
gold.note: corrected down from a stale ~$4,600 read — spot actually eased to ~$4,335 (from ~$4,350 the prior day) even as the Iran conflict escalated further, as dollar firmness + high hike odds outweighed haven demand this time; still well below January's ~$5,300–5,600 record

source.caveat: no free FRED/TE daily series; keep manual or use a market-data API in a later tier

wti.label: WTI Crude
wti.note: kept grinding higher (intraday range ~$89–92) — highest in about three months — as the Hormuz standoff remains unresolved with no ceasefire signal yet
